name: Chitwan & the Central Terai
tagline: Rhino, tiger and Tharu villages in the Terai
meta_description: Chitwan and Central Terai tours: rhino and tiger safaris, Meghauli lodges, Tharu homestays, Parsa, Devghat and Janakpur. Prices, seasons and park fees.
summary: Chitwan, 165 km south-west of Kathmandu, is Nepal's main wildlife region: jeep, canoe and walking safaris for one-horned rhino and Bengal tiger, from Sauraha or Meghauli, in 2–3 nights. The wider Central Terai adds Tharu villages, Parsa National Park and the Hindu pilgrim towns of Devghat and Janakpur. Best months: October–April.
intro: The Central Terai is the flat, hot strip of Nepal between the Churia hills and the Indian border, and Chitwan is its heart. Chitwan National Park, Nepal's first, was created in 1973 and listed by UNESCO in 1984. Its 952 km² of sal forest, elephant grass and river held 694 one-horned rhinos at the 2021 count and 128 tigers at the 2022 survey, alongside sloth bear, gaur, leopard, two kinds of crocodile and more than 500 bird species.

Most visitors base themselves in Sauraha, a village of hotels and safari counters on the north bank of the Rapti, 5–7 hours by road from Kathmandu or a 25-minute flight to Bharatpur plus a 30-minute transfer. Quieter and more expensive, Meghauli on the park's western edge has open grassland, the best birding and Chitwan's top lodges. Two or three nights cover a jeep safari, a dugout canoe ride down the Rapti, a guided walk and an evening of Tharu stick dance.

Beyond the park, the region has more to offer than most itineraries allow for. Barauli, across the Narayani, runs a women-led Tharu homestay. Bishazari Tal, a Ramsar wetland near Bharatpur, is a winter birding site with mugger crocodiles. Devghat, where the Trishuli and Kali Gandaki meet, draws pilgrims and elderly Hindus who retire to its ashrams. To the east, Parsa National Park offers a rougher, almost empty forest of tigers and wild elephants in the Churia hills.

Further east, about 230 km from Kathmandu, Janakpur is identified with the capital of King Janak and the birthplace of Sita. Its white marble Janaki Mandir, completed in 1910, holds one of the most attended evening aartis in Nepal, and Vivah Panchami re-enacts the wedding of Sita and Rama each November or December. Our packages range from 2-night Chitwan safaris and Janakpur darshan trips to luxury lodge stays and combined Chitwan, Lumbini and Kathmandu tours, priced in INR and USD.

highlights.title: One-horned rhinos on the Rapti
highlights.text: Chitwan held 694 of Nepal's 752 greater one-horned rhinos at the 2021 count, and from October to May they are seen on almost every safari. Watch them graze the grassland from a jeep, wade the Rapti from a dugout canoe, or cross to the Sauraha bank at dusk.

highlights.title: Tiger country from Meghauli to Parsa
highlights.text: Chitwan's tigers numbered 128 in the 2022 survey, and daytime sightings near rivers have become more frequent. Full-day jeep drives into the central and western grasslands from February to May give the best odds, and Parsa National Park, adjoining to the east, adds 627 km² of quiet Churia forest.

highlights.title: Canoes, crocodiles and gharial
highlights.text: A 45–60 minute dugout canoe ride on the Rapti passes mugger crocodiles basking on sandbanks, kingfishers and storks, followed by a guided walk back through the forest. The breeding centre at Kasara raises the rare, fish-eating gharial for release into the Narayani and Rapti rivers.

highlights.title: Tharu villages and homestays
highlights.text: The Tharu farmed Chitwan's forests long before the park existed. Cycle through their villages from Sauraha past mud-plastered houses and fish traps, watch the stick dance in the evening, or spend a night at Barauli's women-run homestay, cooking dhikri and fish curry with your hosts.

highlights.title: Birding at Bishazari Tal and Meghauli
highlights.text: Chitwan records more than 500 bird species. Bishazari Tal, a Ramsar wetland since 2003, fills with ducks, storks and raptors from November to March, while Meghauli's grasslands are one of the last strongholds of the Bengal florican, which displays from March to May.

highlights.title: Devghat and Janakpur pilgrimages
highlights.text: Devghat, 7 km north of Narayangarh, is a sacred confluence of ashrams and ghats that fills for Makar Sankranti in January. Janakpur's Janaki Mandir, built in 1910, honours Sita, and its sunset aarti, sacred ponds and Vivah Panchami festival draw pilgrims from across Nepal and India.

getting_there: Bharatpur Airport is the gateway to Chitwan: Buddha Air flies from Kathmandu several times a day in about 25 minutes, and Sauraha is 15 km and 30 minutes away, Meghauli about an hour. By road, Kathmandu to Sauraha is about 165 km and 5–7 hours via Mugling and Narayangarh, and Pokhara is about 150 km and 5–6 hours. From India, Raxaul–Birgunj is the closest border, about 150 km and 4–5 hours via Hetauda, and Sonauli–Bhairahawa is about 165 km and 4–5 hours via Butwal. Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa has limited international flights and domestic links, so check current status before you travel. Janakpur has its own airport, 25 minutes from Kathmandu, and is about 35 km from Jaynagar in Bihar by road or the cross-border railway.
permits: No trekking permits apply in this region. Chitwan National Park charges an entry fee for each day you enter, as we understand it NPR 2,000 for foreign nationals, NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals including Indians and NPR 150 for Nepalis, with a separate fee for vehicles. Parsa National Park follows a similar structure. Visitors must leave the park by dusk, and walking safaris need two licensed guides. Bishazari Tal and the community forests charge small entry fees. Indians need a passport or voter ID; most other nationalities buy a Nepal visa on arrival. Check current status before you travel; our packages include park fees.

months.weather: Sauraha 7 to 22 °C, dry, dense fog until about 10 am
months.summary: January is the coldest month in the Terai. Thick fog sits over the Rapti most mornings and can delay the first flights into Bharatpur, but it lifts to warm, clear afternoons. Grass-cutting season opens views across the grasslands, rhinos are easy to see, and crocodiles bask on the sandbanks. Makar Sankranti in mid-January brings a huge mela to Devghat and a fair to Dhanusadham, and Tharu villages celebrate Maghi, their new year, with feasts and dancing.
months.tip: Book late-morning flights to Bharatpur and pack a fleece for open jeeps before the fog clears.

months.summary: February is the best all-round month for Chitwan. The grass has been cut and burned in patches, the mornings are cool rather than cold, and rhinos graze in the open with young calves. Tiger odds rise as water sources shrink. Migratory birds are still present at Bishazari Tal, and Meghauli's grasslands are at their most productive. In Janakpur, days are comfortable for temple visits, and the Mithila parikrama often begins on the new moon in late February or March.
months.tip: Book a full-day jeep safari this month; visibility in the cut grassland makes the long drive worthwhile.

months.summary: March brings warm, dry days and some of the best wildlife viewing of the year. Animals gather at the remaining waterholes and oxbow lakes, sloth bears and gaur become more active, and the Bengal florican begins its displays in the Meghauli grasslands. Parsa's sal forest is pleasant before the heat builds. Holi and Ram Navami may fall this month, the second bringing crowds to Janakpur's Ram Mandir, and the parikrama ends at Holi in Janakpur.
months.tip: Start safaris at first light and plan pool time or a rest between 11 am and 3 pm.

months.weather: Sauraha 19 to 35 °C, hot and dry, hazy
months.summary: April is hot, with afternoons around 35 °C and hazy skies, but it is peak season for tigers: the grass is short, water is scarce and big cats are seen along the Rapti and Reu. Rhinos wallow in pools through the day. Activities run early and late, with rest at midday. Janakpur passes 37 °C, though Ram Navami or Sita Navami can draw pilgrims. Nepali New Year in mid-April brings domestic visitors to Sauraha.
months.tip: Choose a resort with air conditioning and a pool, and carry 2 litres of water on every safari.

months.weather: Sauraha 23 to 36 °C, up to 40 °C, humid, pre-monsoon storms
months.summary: May is the hottest month, with highs of 36–40 °C and rising humidity before the monsoon. Wildlife viewing remains good for those who can handle the heat, and rhinos spend long hours in water. Evening thunderstorms arrive late in the month. Lodges cut rates and Indian school-holiday families arrive. Keep outdoor time to the first three hours after sunrise and the late afternoon, and avoid Janakpur, where days often pass 38 °C.
months.tip: Book the 6 am jeep slot and a canoe ride for the cooler early hour.

months.weather: Sauraha 25 to 34 °C, monsoon arrives mid-month, humid
months.summary: The monsoon usually reaches Chitwan in mid-June. Until then, safaris continue in heavy heat; afterwards, the Rapti rises, park tracks start to close and the grass grows quickly. Most core-zone jeep safaris and canoe rides stop or shrink, and activities move to the buffer zone and community forests. Some lodges in Meghauli close for the season. Rice planting begins in Tharu villages, which makes a village walk around Sauraha or Barauli worthwhile.
months.tip: If you travel in June, go in the first half of the month and confirm which activities your lodge is still running.

months.weather: Sauraha 25 to 32 °C, heavy monsoon rain, very humid
months.summary: July is the wettest month. Heavy rain floods the Rapti and Narayani, most of Chitwan's core zone is closed to visitors, and leeches and mosquitoes are everywhere in the forest. Landslides on the Mugling–Narayangarh road can cause delays of hours. A few Sauraha hotels stay open at low rates with buffer-zone walks and village visits, and Devghat's ashrams and Bharatpur's riverfront remain open. For wildlife, wait for October.
months.tip: Fly to Bharatpur rather than drive if you must travel in July, and check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Sauraha 25 to 32 °C, monsoon rain, very humid
months.summary: August stays wet, hot and green. Park safaris remain closed or limited to short buffer-zone routes, and Parsa and the Meghauli lodges are largely shut. Rhinos sometimes move into the fields around Sauraha, and resident birds are active between showers. Janakpur is humid and occasionally flooded but quiet. Prices are at their lowest of the year, though roads can be blocked and outdoor plans often change with the weather.
months.tip: Pack a light rain jacket, leech socks and quick-dry clothes, and keep plans flexible.

months.weather: Sauraha 24 to 32 °C, rain easing late in the month
months.summary: The monsoon weakens through September, and park tracks reopen late in the month as the Rapti falls, though dates depend on each year's rain. The landscape is intensely green and the grass at its tallest, so canoe rides and riverside walks give better views than jeep drives. Hotels reopen with low-season rates. It is a sensible month for a short Sauraha stay combined with Devghat and Bishazari Tal, but not for serious tiger seekers.
months.tip: Plan Chitwan for the last ten days of September, when more of the park is usually open.

months.weather: Sauraha 19 to 31 °C, clear and dry after the monsoon
months.summary: October brings clear skies, fresh green forest and the start of the main season. The grass is still tall, so rhinos are best seen from canoes and along the riverbanks, while tiger sightings are less frequent than in spring. Dashain and Tihar fill Sauraha with Nepali families, and Chhath, after Diwali, is a major festival at Janakpur's ponds. Book early for Diwali week, when Indian visitors arrive in large numbers.
months.tip: Reserve Diwali and Dashain dates six to eight weeks ahead, as mid-range resorts sell out.

months.weather: Sauraha 13 to 28 °C, dry, clear, cool mornings
months.summary: November is one of the most comfortable months, with dry, sunny days and cool mornings. The first migratory birds arrive at Bishazari Tal and the oxbow lakes, crocodiles begin basking, and rhino sightings are reliable. Janakpur is pleasant for darshan and evening aarti, and in some years Vivah Panchami falls in late November. A week here combines a Chitwan safari, Devghat and Janakpur without heat or rain.
months.tip: Add a dawn birding walk at Bishazari Tal to a Sauraha stay; November mornings are crisp and clear.

months.weather: Sauraha 8 to 24 °C, dry, foggy mornings from mid-month
months.summary: December is cool and dry, with fog building in the second half of the month that can sit over the Terai until mid-morning. Rhinos and crocodiles are easy to find, and winter birds fill the wetlands. Vivah Panchami fills Janakpur, falling on 14 December in 2026, and the Chitwan Elephant and Tourism Festival runs in Sauraha in late December. Christmas and New Year are the busiest weeks of the year, so book early.
months.tip: Bring a warm jacket and hat for early safaris, when open jeeps feel close to freezing in the mist.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Chitwan?
faqs.a: Two nights is the minimum and three nights is ideal. Two nights give you one jeep safari, a canoe ride, a short walk and the Tharu dance. Three nights add a full-day jeep drive, which greatly improves tiger and sloth bear chances, or a split stay in Meghauli. Birders and photographers should plan four nights, including Bishazari Tal.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Chitwan National Park?
faqs.a: October to April is the season. February to April is best for rhino and tiger, because the grass has been cut and animals gather at water. October and November are green and comfortable, December and January are cool with foggy mornings, and May is very hot. From mid-June to mid-September monsoon floods close most of the park.

faqs.q: How do I reach Chitwan from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Fly to Bharatpur in about 25 minutes and transfer 30 minutes to Sauraha, or drive about 165 km in 5–7 hours via Mugling and Narayangarh. Tourist buses leave Kathmandu around 7 am and reach Sauraha in the early afternoon for NPR 800–1,200. A private car allows stops at Manakamana or for rafting on the Trishuli.

faqs.q: Is Chitwan open during the monsoon?
faqs.a: Partly. From mid-June to mid-September floods close most of the core zone, so jeep safaris and canoe rides stop or move to the buffer zone and community forests. Some Meghauli lodges close, while many Sauraha hotels stay open at low rates. Roads can be blocked by landslides. Opening dates depend on the rains, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the Chitwan National Park entry fee?
faqs.a: As we understand it, the daily entry fee is NPR 2,000 for foreign nationals, NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals including Indians and NPR 150 for Nepalis, charged for each day you enter the park. Vehicles pay a separate fee. Activity costs such as jeeps and canoes are extra. Fees change, so check current status before you travel; our packages include them.

faqs.q: What is the Chitwan tour package cost from India?
faqs.a: Our Chitwan packages start from about ₹16,000 per person for 2 nights with a tourist bus from Kathmandu, about ₹22,000 for 3 nights by private car, and over ₹1,10,000 for a luxury Meghauli lodge with flights, on twin sharing. Travel from India is extra: overland via Raxaul or Sonauli costs far less than flying to Kathmandu.

faqs.q: Should I stay in Sauraha or Meghauli?
faqs.a: Stay in Sauraha for value, choice and convenience: dozens of hotels, cafes and Tharu dance shows within walking distance of the river. Choose Meghauli for open grassland, better birding, fewer vehicles and full-board luxury lodges such as Meghauli Serai and Barahi Jungle Lodge. On a three-night trip, splitting two nights in Sauraha and one in Meghauli works well.

faqs.q: Is Chitwan good for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes. Children enjoy jeep safaris, canoe rides, the Elephant Breeding Centre and the Tharu dance, and many resorts have pools and vegetarian menus. Choose half-day activities for under-tens, as full-day drives are long and hot. Guides may set a minimum age for walking safaris, so check before booking. October to March is the most comfortable season.

faqs.q: Can I combine Janakpur with a Chitwan trip?
faqs.a: Yes, though they are about 280 km and 7–8 hours apart by road via Hetauda. Most travellers either drive between them with a stop at Devghat, or fly Kathmandu–Janakpur and Kathmandu–Bharatpur as separate legs. Allow two nights in Janakpur for darshan, aarti and Dhanusadham, and two or three nights in Chitwan.
